I’m the CEO of Izypeo, a SaaS platform helping organizations digitalize and simplify their Quality, Health, Safety and Environmental processes.
We help organizations — particularly multi-site operations — centralize field data, automate workflows and action plans, manage risks and compliance, and turn QHSE data into actionable insights.
We continuously invest in new technologies, including AI, to make QHSE management simpler, smarter and more efficient.
As CEO, I focus on vision, product strategy, customer value and growth, while staying close to the people who use our platform every day.
Our ambition is to build a new generation of QHSE software, combining technology, data and intelligent automation to help organizations improve the way they manage their QHSE processes.
I’m always interested in connecting with QHSE leaders, operational teams, technology partners and organizations looking to transform the way they manage QHSE.
Feel free to connect or message me — I’d be happy to exchange ideas.

Mon moteur ? Comprendre et façonner l'impact profond de la technologie. Non pas la technologie pour elle-même, mais pour ce qu'elle change. L'impact de l'IA sur le métier de développeur, qui se réinvente sous nos yeux, mais aussi l'impact, plus silencieux, de nos choix techniques sur l'environnement et la société.

En tant que CTO, je traduis cette passion en action. Je crois en une technologie "bien faite", où l'excellence en ingénierie et en architecture n'est pas un but, mais la fondation solide qui nous permet de créer avec plaisir et sérénité. C'est sur ce socle que je bâtis ma plus grande fierté : les équipes.

Mon plus grand accomplissement  est de bâtir et de faire grandir des organisations techniques performantes, à grande échelle. Cela implique de dénicher les bons talents, mais surtout de créer le cadre — structure, carrières, management — où chacun peut s'épanouir.

Aujourd'hui, je souhaite transmettre et échanger sur deux fronts qui me semblent cruciaux :

🔹 Pour les développeurs et les leaders techniques : Comment transformer la montée en puissance de l'IA en une opportunité exceptionnelle ? Comment l'utiliser pour augmenter notre savoir-faire, notre créativité et notre impact, tout en gardant une approche critique et éthique.

🌱 Pour tous les acteurs de la tech : Comment faire de la sobriété numérique et du Green IT une évidence ? Je suis convaincu que cet engagement doit être au cœur de nos métiers, pour construire une technologie non seulement performante, mais aussi responsable.

Ces transformations soulèvent d'immenses questions. Si ces sujets vous interpellent, n'hésitez pas à me suivre ou à me contacter pour que nous puissions échanger et apprendre ensemble.

projects.title: Disaster Relief
projects.description:
Disaster relief was a concept rising out of the recent Colorado floods. The goal was to connect people in need with relief organizations and volunteers who were in a position to help. This project was part of Denver Startup Weekend 5 (Sept. 13-15, 2013) and was successfully launched and made available for the relief efforts.

The solution involved a web page where people in need could register their needs. Yet we also leveraged Twilio to provide an SMS (i.e. texting) capability where people could text in their needs and have that recorded in the system. In addition, relief organizations could log in and work through the queue of needs and marshall volunteers to help those in need.

The solution included:
• a web front end built with HTML/CSS/Javascript
• a REST API built in Ruby/Rails; hosted on heroku with postgresql as the database
• a Node.js tier that handled integration between Twilio and the REST API (for SMS conversations)
• Twilio integration providing SMS conversation capabilities

My role was helping develop the REST API leveraging Ruby and Rails.

publications.title: Dwell Time prediction in a container terminal
publications.description:
Container terminals play a pivotal role in logistics chains as they serve as a vital connection point between sea-based transportation and inland transportation modes. Enhancing operations will lead to more improved resource allocation, reduced congestion, enhanced customer satisfaction, and increased overall efficiency. 

This paper presents an approach for dwell time prediction in a container terminal, highlighting the significance of accurate predictions and the challenges associated with this task. 
The aim is to develop a forecasting tool that can aid yard planners and terminal operators in their daily decision-making processes, specifically in determining stacking policies and optimizing the allocation of containers, equipment and human resources.

publications.title: A Large Neighborhood Search approach for the Daily Drayage Problem with Time Windows (DDPTW)
publications.description:
As part of intermodal transportation, drayage operations are movements of empty and full
containers in the hinterland area of an intermodal terminal. We consider a truck company
owning a fleet of trucks and that receives a set of import and export missions from different
clients to fulfill. The trucks start their journey from the truck company yard and execute the
assigned missions by moving containers between different locations (depots where containers
are stored, industrial customers and terminals) while respecting the associated time windows.
This problem is known as the Daily Drayage Problem with Time Windows (DDPTW).

The problem can be seen as a generalization of the Pickup and Delivery Problem with
Time Windows (PDPTW). In addition to the traditional PDP constraints, composed requests
introduce minimum time-lag constraints between pairs of pickup and delivery requests. Since
solving the Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MIP) formulation of the DDPTW using a
standard solver cannot scale on large instances, we propose a Large Neighborhood Search
(LNS) heuristic.

Written by IMT professors Nabil Absi, Dominique Feillet, Thierry Garaix + DMSLOG.AI PhDs Cyriac Azefack, Taki Eddine Korabi, and doctoral student Diana Abi-Nader.
